correctness.rationale: The statement is about the Euclidean derivative inverse of a single planar cell, not an end-to-end solver. AP has positive real eigenvalues by SPD similarity, so J=I+AP is invertible, and nonexpansivity is equivalent to JᵀJ−I⪰0. In r-aligned coordinates, u,v>0 imply positive trace for this symmetric test matrix, so its determinant is decisive. With d=ατ, S=α+τ, D=α−τ, z=cos 2θ, and K=(1−γ)²D²/4, direct expansion gives dγ[4+S(1+γ)+γd]−dγD(1−γ)z−K(1−z²). If D=0 this is positive. Otherwise completing the square gives the advertised vertex z₀=2dγ/[D(1−γ)] and minimum F=dγ[4+S(1+γ)]−K. If z₀≥1, then K≤dγD(1−γ)/2, which implies F>0 because S>D and γ>0. Thus every negative or zero unconstrained minimum is physically attained. F increases strictly in γ with F(0)<0<F(1), proving the threshold and all strict and equality cases. Independent fractional arithmetic gives det(JᵀJ−I)=−2853/2000 and det(sym J)=123591/40000 in the rational example, and direct bisection gives γ*=0.0542649822871. The checked example shows monotonicity is not a contraction test for the same pair. Frozen verify_inverse_frontier.py was inspected, not executed; finite samples do not establish the continuum result.

evidence: Cibicki et al. eq. (13) gives an exact angle-by-angle determinant for the symmetric part of the normalized single-cell Jacobian. Its trace is positive, making the determinant a complete sign test. Eq. (14) is a weaker condition obtained without the vacuum term and is not relied on here.

The classical Jordan-product papers by Strang and by Alikakos–Bates are plausible general alternate coverage, but only bibliographic/landing material was accessible; their exact theorems were not verified. Moll et al. §III-C addresses inversion in an energy-based hysteresis model, not a covering vector-play result.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The exact pointwise formula covers more than an all-angle threshold: it resolves the sign at any specified relative angle after the reciprocal reparameterization. No unverified general Jordan-product theorem is needed for the coverage decision.

evidence: Eq. (13), with A_c,P_c above, evaluates det(I+sym(A_cP_c)) as 1+tr(A_cP_c)+det(A_cP_c)−(1−γ)²(α_c−τ_c)²(1−z²)/16. Multiply by (dγ)² via the congruence. Substituting α_c+τ_c=2S/(dγ), α_c−τ_c=2D/(dγ) and α_cτ_c=4/(dγ²) gives exactly dγ[4+S(1+γ)+γd]−dγD(1−γ)z−(1−γ)²D²(1−z²)/4, the frozen angular polynomial.

Completing the square removes γ²d² and leaves F as the minimum. If that value is nonpositive, z₀ is inside (0,1); the commuting orientations have positive determinant. The strict parameter crossing follows by differentiation. The rational example applies the two known pointwise tests, at the original and reciprocal pair, and provides a witness but not a separate general result.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The exact prior determinant, congruence and elementary one-variable minimization recover the boundary, the equality angle and the strict alternatives without any additional constitutive lemma. Neither replacing a forward metric with this equivalent reciprocal criterion nor giving an illustrative rational specialization evades that implication.

evidence: For X=AP, JᵀJ−I=Xᵀ[I+X⁻¹+X⁻ᵀ]X. Thus the norm criterion, with either strictness or equality, is equivalent by congruence to I+2sym(A⁻¹P⁻¹)⪰0.

Put A_c=(2/γ)A⁻¹ and P_c=γP⁻¹. Then I+sym(A_c P_c)=I+2sym(A⁻¹P⁻¹). The spectra of A_c are 2/(γτ)≥2/(γα)>0 and those of P_c are 1,γ. In dimension two the preferred eigenvectors for both factors switch to their orthogonal directions; z=cos 2θ is unchanged when both are switched.
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: The same-pair distinction between monotonicity and inverse nonexpansivity is true but does not rule out exact reciprocal equivalence. The reciprocal pair is in the very same planar SPD family and ranges over the same orientations; no extra vector-play restriction blocks the substitution into eq. (13).

originality.rationale: The inverse test is exactly the published pointwise vector-play monotonicity test at a reciprocal, rescaled pair. The same prior angular determinant polynomial then gives the entire threshold and attaining orientation by routine completion of the square. This is positive coverage by implication, not an assertion that the paper states the inverse theorem verbatim, and not an inference from the unrelated unshifted monotonicity sufficient condition or positive eigenvalues.
residual_risks: Exact theorems and attainment in the two classical Jordan-product sources were not retrieved and are not attributed here. Eq. (13) and the explicit reduction are sufficient for the positive coverage finding.
The generic singular-value keyword search returned no close primary source; that is not evidence of novelty or whole-literature noncoverage.

value.rationale: Inverse conditioning is well motivated in a local magnetic constitutive solve, and the rational witness is pedagogically useful. However, the frozen frontier is the elementary all-angle envelope of an existing exact pointwise formula at reciprocal parameters. The extra example is a routine specialization of those tests, not a distinct structural witness requiring a new argument. As a standalone finding it supplies no nonmechanical boundary or extra Newton/constitutive consequence; that limitation, not the narrow planar scope itself, drives this verdict.
